name: atlantis-d163012f-blind30
instr:
# Diagnosing a Broken Atlantis Server Without a Test Suite

The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. What follows is everything I could pin down from the outside, in the order I stumbled into it.

It watches pull requests and turns comments on them into infrastructure changes, and I can only describe what I saw from the outside. Standing it up from a hand-written operator settings file already goes wrong three ways. A file that hands two repository entries the full set of per-repository options at once is read into something that does not match what the file says, while entries setting only one option each are read as they always were. The per-repository list naming which stages must stay quiet on a pull request is no longer looked at: a word outside the two supported ones is swallowed silently instead of being refused with the message that names the supported values. And in the list of path patterns saying which directories to leave out when it works out projects for itself, a pattern that cannot be compiled — a lone opening bracket, or a trailing backslash — and a pattern beginning with a slash are all accepted with no error, though an unrecognised mode word in the same block is still refused.
